cites.quote: The design adds an `onDuty` array to GET /api/dashboard.
In the MVP every request is the actor `staff` and every permission is granted.
HMS-23: one doctor on duty today, counted as the day schedule counts. No contact details (DSH-9).
never request bodies, contact details or medical
log the route and the error message only, never request bodies or patient data.
checked by the HMS-23 REQ-13 API test
HMS-23 REQ-2, REQ-3, REQ-13: lists each doctor on duty with name, department, counts and next free slot, and nothing else

findings.suggested_fix: Add a claim citing sample-system:api/test/dashboard-on-duty.test.ts#L50 and reference it in the Known REQ-13 line.
findings.text: Known REQ-13 says it is checked by the HMS-23 REQ-13 API test but cites only C5 (the type). The test exists at api/test/dashboard-on-duty.test.ts L50 and should be cited.

rubric_items.reason: No new route, permission kept, bound SQL parameter, no contact fields, escaped React output and no new logging all checked against code; the per-doctor query cost (1 + 2N queries per load) is found. I found no missed weakness.
Every claim and SF-1 cite the exact lines: doctorService.ts L177-L178, doctorRepo.ts L186/L191, dashboard.ts L10, types.ts L83, DashboardPage.tsx L92.
SF-1 rated minor fits: an internal staff dashboard with a bounded doctor count, read-only queries, and no exposure or bypass.
SF-1 gives a clear direction (one query each for blocks and appointments by an array of doctor ids). It does not name the repo methods to add.
No false positives; the single finding is real in the code at doctorRepo.ts L190-L191 and doctorService.ts L177-L178.
